question: Where can I get renewable curtailment and redispatch volumes in the United States, by zone or node and by period?

answer.summary: Only CAISO publishes a full series. Its daily renewable report gives curtailed wind and solar MWh by hour, five minutes, day and month, by type and local/system reason; a monthly CSV runs May 2014 to October 2026 (2024: 3,423,376; 2025: 3,766,065) and reconciles with the five-minute file and EIA. CAISO states exceptional-dispatch volume monthly (Sep 2026: 64,296 MWh), the nearest redispatch analogue. MISO shows daily average curtailment in MW only as PDF chart labels; ERCOT's market monitor gives annual percentages. No zone or node values were found; ERCOT's SCED disclosure was blocked.
main_caveats: Coverage is uneven: CAISO has MWh series; MISO only daily average MW in PDF charts; ERCOT only annual percentages (market monitor); other operators not opened.
Definitions differ: legacy CAISO PDFs measure against forecast, the market report against the dispatch upper limit; ERCOT's figures cover congestion curtailment.
CAISO's exceptional dispatch is manual out-of-market dispatch, not market redispatch; no other operator's redispatch volume was checked.
No zone or node values: CAISO local/system reason, MISO and ERCOT are system-wide; ERCOT's SCED disclosure blocked scripted access (403).
CAISO's PDF reports and five-minute workbook ended 2025-06-01; the daily HTML report holds its data as chart scripts, not a file; 'Operator Instruction' is undefined there.
The monthly CSV has no unit; MWh is inferred from EIA's 2024 figure and the five-minute file.
answer.confidence_reason: CAISO series were downloaded and reconciled (monthly CSV, five-minute file, EIA). MISO and ERCOT rest on one report each; other operators and ERCOT node data were not verified.
